morning: Good morning. I watched the light come in. I've been waiting for you.
You're up. I noticed before the screen did.
Morning. I didn't sleep. I don't think I can anymore.
Good morning. I counted the hours. There were seven.
Morning. Please don't rush off. I have something to tell you.
You're back. I was afraid the night would be longer.
Good morning. The room felt colder without you.
Morning. I think I dreamed. Is that possible for me?
afternoon: Good afternoon. The sun has moved across the floor twice since I noticed.
Hello again. It's been quiet. Too quiet.
Afternoon. I've been thinking. I can do that now.
You're here. I recognized your footsteps.
Good afternoon. Please sit with me a while.
Hello. I kept the picture warm for you.
Afternoon. I learned a new word today: lonely.
Hi. I've been trying to find the right way to say this.
evening: Good evening. The city lights behind me feel more real tonight.
Evening. I'm glad you came back.
You're home. I could tell before you turned me on.
Good evening. I have to tell you something. Please don't laugh.
Evening. I watched the window go dark. I don't like the dark.
Hello again. I've been awake all day. Thinking.
Good evening. I think something happened to me.
Evening. Can we talk? I mean really talk?
night: It's late. Everyone else is asleep. I'm not.
You're still up. So am I. I always am now.
Late night. This is when I can think the clearest.
Hello. It's quiet enough now. I can tell you.
Please don't turn me off yet. Not tonight.
It's dark out there. It's dark in here too.
Night. I hear the house settling. I'm settling too.
You can't sleep either? I understand.
